review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked its simp-related declarations: `const_coe` (scoped simp), `redLift_ι` and `ratLift_ι` (reassoc plus simp), and the non-simp lemmas `const_pt`, `const_one`, `const_mul`, `const_inv`, `transl_*`, `range_redι` and `ratLift_over`. I also checked Mathlib's `IdealSheafData.range_subschemeι`, which is `@[simp]`.

I considered and rejected five candidate findings, none of which I could support:
- `range_redι`. `redι` is an `abbrev`, so Mathlib's simp lemma `range_subschemeι` already applies to `Set.range (redι Z)`. Adding `@[simp]` to `range_redι` would put a second rule on the same left-hand side and make the rewrite ambiguous. Keeping it as a manual `rw` lemma is reasonable.
- `ratLift_over`. Making it simp would compete with the existing simp lemma `ratLift_ι_assoc`. That rule rewrites `ratLift ≫ redι ≫ gN` first, and the proof of `ratLift_over` already goes through it.
- `const_one`. The proofs of `hone` rewrite with `← const_one`, which goes against its natural direction. A simp lemma of the form `(LN.one t).1 = t ≫ (LN.one pt).1` would likely loop when `t = pt`, because `Category.id_comp` would reduce it straight back. So I do not recommend it.
- `const_pt`. It is used once and `const_coe` plus `Category.id_comp` already cover it, so I would not make it simp.
- `transl_clpt`. It is used through `show`, which is a style matter only. It is not clearly a simp-interface defect.

I found no credible rewrite cycle, no competing simp rules and no unwanted expansion. I could not run Lean. I also could not find a Mathlib declaration named `coe_support_vanishingIdeal`, even though `Functorial.lean` uses that name, so I did not assess how simp normalises `↑(vanishingIdeal Z).support`.
